title: Normalized finite integral extension of the root-limit Tate line
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite intermediate extension of Q_l in its fixed algebraic closure, and X a scheme on which l is invertible. For integralMap:Z_l -> O_E and the actual root-limit transition integralLineMap of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-maps], there exists an Endpoint [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-endpoints] from zlLine(l,X) to spIntegralTwist(X,l,E). In particular the semilinear map has exactly the prescribed underlying root transition, its derived scalar adjoint is an isomorphism, and its transpose is the single-image semilinear map followed by the inverse restriction/single comparison. No diagram, class, trace, or direct-image comparison is asserted.

source.place: paragraph (1), finite free extension commutes with the root inverse limit

proof.text: The base coefficient condensed identification proves that the actual bottom integralMap is invertible. Restrict the integral locally free line along this monoidal equivalence. SignedLineTensorEquivalence and InternalSectionModuleFlat prove flatness of zlLine; invertibility in residue fields follows from hX by the residue homomorphism.

Apply the finite integral basis theorem to bottomField <= E. Restrict its basis along the bottom coefficient isomorphism and identify the composite coefficient map with integralMap by its pointwise formula. FiniteFreeScalarCoordinates identifies scalar extension followed by restriction with the finite power functor. Finite powers preserve all limits, and the forgetful functor reflects limits. Hence integral scalar extension preserves the root tower limit.

Use diagonalIntegral_rootLevelScalars for the natural isomorphism of finite towers with its scalar-unit formula. Restriction and scalar extension preserve the source limiting cone, and postcomposing by this natural isomorphism preserves its limit property. The unique isomorphism between this cone and the target limit is the ordinary scalar comparison. Its projection equations, naturality of the ordinary extension unit, and the finite-level normalization show that its composite with the unit is exactly integralLineMap.

Apply diagonal_flat_scalar_endpoint_iso to zlLine. Compose its isomorphism with the single-image ordinary comparison. Its semilinear map is the ordinary scalar unit followed by restriction of that comparison, and the previous projection argument identifies its underlying map with integralLineMap. Naturality of the derived adjunction Hom equivalence and the restriction/single comparison gives precisely Endpoint.normalization.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (1); implemented finite-basis limit preservation, passage from normalized finite levels to root limits, source flatness, and derived adjunction normalization. Only the positive finite-level tensor comparison remains split off.

theorem diagonalFinite_integralEndpoint
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsUnit (l : Γ(X, ⊤))) :
    Nonempty (Endpoint (integralMap l E) (zlLine l X) (spIntegralTwist X l E)
      (integralLineMap l E X))
